Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-prompt-long-0119", "row_sha256": "a21deea28e73b4fb8b610efce955e101e27cb1f3550be007e2294b4bbf31530d", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "need a prompt for drafting an email to Copperline Rehearsal Rooms about a rehearsal booking for North Window. We are a five piece indie band based near the east end, and we need a proper full band practice before our small hall show the following week. This is only an inquiry and an email draft, not a booking being made. Jo Park is the person coordinating for us; no email address or phone number is in my notes so don't make one up or put in fake contact details. Keep the message friendly and practical, not salesy. It should sound like a real band asking a rehearsal place questions, and not like we already have the room.

Our first choice is Thursday, October 15, 2026, from 6:30 to 9:30 p.m. We'd need the full three hours, not a setup hour before that. If Thursday can't work, Friday, October 16, at the same time is the one fallback we have agreed to ask about. Don't turn that into a request for both nights, or imply that Friday is booked. We are trying to keep the total room cost at or below $180 including tax and any mandatory fees. No one has approved a higher amount. We don't know the hourly rate, tax, deposit, or whether there are additional charges, so have the email ask for an itemized total and say what amount is due to reserve the room and by when. Don't say we are paying a deposit now.

Room size matters because all five of us and our cases have to fit, and our guitarist needs room to set up a pedalboard. We were told Room B is about 16 by 18 feet, but I don't know whether that measurement includes a doorway or gear shelf. We need a room with at least 10-foot ceilings because Len wants to set overhead microphones and cymbals without hitting anything. Ask them to confirm the usable floor dimensions and ceiling height for the room they suggest. Room A came up in an old conversation, but we have not been told its dimensions and it might have a lower ceiling; don't describe it as suitable. If there isn't a room meeting the ceiling requirement on either date, ask what the next Thursday evening with a room that does meet it would be. That's not permission to accept a shorter ceiling.

There are five people: Jo Park sings and plays guitar, Len Ortiz is drums, Mara Velez plays bass, Devon Price plays guitar, and Kit Bell sings and plays keys. We need a room where the five of us can rehearse together; don't turn this into a drum lesson or a recording session. Len will bring his snare, kick pedal, sticks and overhead microphones. Mara can bring the cymbals, but has no cymbal stands. I wrote this down from the phone conversation: the receptionist said, "The room is yours only after the deposit clears." I also have the venue's message: "Backline includes a five-piece kit, one throne, and a basic hardware pack." Mara's exact note to me was, "I can bring the cymbals, but not the stands." Keep those words exactly if the email mentions the notes, and don't claim the basic hardware pack definitely includes cymbal stands. Ask what hardware is included and whether anything else is needed for the cymbals. We have a guitar amp and bass amp between us but I haven't confirmed their sizes, so don't list models or promise the amps are enough.

Len also sent this: "Please don't book the room with the low ceiling; my overheads won't fit." That is a real constraint, not a quote to wave away. Don't present a lower-ceiling room as an acceptable alternative or say the overhead microphones are optional. Mention the 10-foot minimum clearly, while asking the venue to verify it rather than treating our old Room B measurement as confirmation. No one has picked a preferred microphone setup beyond Len bringing the overheads.

A few logistics we want covered in the message, without making it a long list of demands:
1. Confirm whether the listed times are available on the first-choice date and, only if not, whether the fallback date is available.
2. Confirm the actual room dimensions and ceiling height, and whether the kit and hardware quoted above are in the room for that booking.
3. Give the full price including required tax and fees, plus the deposit amount and payment deadline; keep our $180 maximum clear.
4. Ask about load-in and parking for unloading the drum and guitar gear, and ask what the cancellation or date-change policy is.
5. Don't ask them to hold either date unless we've said we want that. We're not ready to authorize a reservation; first Jo needs the facts to share with the band.

Jo remembers the receptionist saying, "The room is yours only after the deposit clears." Please don't rewrite that as a confirmed booking or say the venue has accepted us. We need to know the actual terms, since that remark doesn't tell us the deposit amount or deadline. If they can meet the ceiling, timing and price conditions, the email can ask what the next step would be, but it must remain an inquiry. If none of those options works, ask for the next qualifying Thursday evening rather than inventing another date or settling for a room that won't fit the setup.

Please make the resulting email easy for Jo to review and send: put the preferred and fallback dates in clear order, keep the room requirements and budget easy to spot, and retain the quoted remarks exactly if included. Don't insert a greeting with an invented recipient name, a signature with invented contact details, or any claim that a date is available. The ending should ask for the information needed to decide, not announce that we accept a room, a price, or a deposit term. If something isn't in these notes, leave it as an unanswered question rather than guessing. The email should cover the complete request, including the next-Thursday fallback condition, and finish with a useful closing question to the venue.", "output": "Write a friendly, practical email draft from Jo Park, coordinating for the five-piece indie band North Window, to Copperline Rehearsal Rooms. This is an inquiry only: do not make a booking, request a hold, or imply that the venue has accepted the band or that any date is available. Do not invent a recipient name, contact details, or other missing information. Keep the email natural and not salesy.

The band needs a full-band rehearsal before a small hall show the following week. Their preferred booking is Thursday, October 15, 2026, from 6:30 to 9:30 p.m. If that date is unavailable, ask whether Friday, October 16, 2026, at the same time is available. Do not request both nights or imply that the fallback date is booked. If neither date has a room meeting the ceiling requirement below, ask for the next Thursday evening when a qualifying room is available; do not invent a date or accept a room with a lower ceiling.

State the room requirements clearly. All five band members and their cases need to fit, with space for a guitarist's pedalboard. The band requires ceilings of at least 10 feet so Len can set up overhead microphones and cymbals. Room B was described in old notes as about 16 by 18 feet, but that measurement is unconfirmed and may include a doorway or gear shelf. Ask the venue to confirm the usable floor dimensions and ceiling height of the room it suggests. Room A's dimensions and ceiling height are unknown, so do not describe it as suitable. Len's overhead microphones are not optional. Preserve his exact note if quoted: "Please don't book the room with the low ceiling; my overheads won't fit."

North Window has five members: Jo Park sings and plays guitar; Len Ortiz plays drums; Mara Velez plays bass; Devon Price plays guitar; and Kit Bell sings and plays keys. This is a full-band rehearsal, not a drum lesson or a recording session. Len will bring his snare, kick pedal, sticks, and overhead microphones. Mara can bring cymbals but has no cymbal stands. The venue's message says, "Backline includes a five-piece kit, one throne, and a basic hardware pack." Ask what hardware is included and whether anything else is needed for the cymbals; do not assume that the basic hardware pack includes cymbal stands. Mara's exact note is, "I can bring the cymbals, but not the stands." The band has a guitar amp and a bass amp, but their sizes are unconfirmed; do not list models or claim the amps are sufficient.

The total room cost must be no more than $180, including tax and any mandatory fees. No higher price has been approved. The hourly rate, taxes, deposit, and other possible charges are unknown, so ask for an itemized total and the amount due to reserve the room, including the payment deadline. Do not say that the band is paying a deposit now. The receptionist's exact remark was, "The room is yours only after the deposit clears." Preserve those exact words if you include the remark, and do not turn it into a claim that the room is confirmed or that the band has agreed to the terms.

In a concise, well-organized message, ask the venue to:
1. Confirm availability for the preferred date and, only if it is unavailable, the fallback date.
2. Confirm the suggested room's usable floor dimensions, ceiling height, and whether the quoted kit and hardware will be available for the booking.
3. Provide the full price, including required tax and fees, and state the deposit amount and payment deadline. Make the $180 maximum clear.
4. Explain load-in and parking arrangements for unloading drum and guitar gear, and provide the cancellation or date-change policy.

The band is not ready to authorize a reservation; Jo first needs the details to share with the band. If the venue can meet the timing, ceiling, and price conditions, ask what the next step would be without accepting a room, price, or deposit term. End by asking for the information needed to decide. Keep all quoted remarks exactly as written if included, and leave anything not established in these notes as a question rather than guessing."}]
